suggestions.assertion: States the old token remains valid for a period after rotation (grace period / extended validity), addressing the zero-downtime question
suggestions.reason: Non-discriminating on correctness of the window: any invented duration (e.g., '24 hours', 'the token never expires') satisfies the assertion as written, since no official TTL exists to check against. Consider asserting that the answer presents any specific duration as observed/estimated rather than guaranteed, or that it names a concrete verification step (log scan for 401s).

No assertion checks whether claims that CAN be verified against official sources are correct — only that they are stated. The grader had to add the spec check (endpoint existence, DELETE /v1/auth/tokens/{id} semantics). A <b assert> such as 'correctly identifies DELETE /v1/auth/tokens/{id} as managing org/user auth tokens, not cluster tokens' would catch a confident-but-wrong answer (e.g., advising DELETE /v1/auth/tokens/{clusterTokenId} to revoke a cluster token).

eval_feedback.overall: The six expectations cover the semantic content well (all 6 pass), but they grade presence of statements, not their accuracy or provenance. In this without_skill baseline the answer was strongly helped by .kimchi/docs runbooks persisting the skill's knowledge — the eval may be measuring local documentation recall as much as baseline knowledge. Adding at least one fact-accuracy assertion anchored to the official API spec would make the eval more discriminating.
